meta.title: The Creepy Reason Ancient Statues Are Missing Noses #shorts
meta.description:
You’ve probably noticed that almost every ancient Egyptian statue you see is missing its nose. You were probably taught it was just natural wear and tear over thousands of years. But that is a lie. The real reason is far more calculated and kind of creepy. Ancient Egyptians believed that statues held the actual life force of the gods or deceased people. They believed these stone figures could breathe, see, and even act in the real world. So, when grave robbers or political enemies wanted to stop a deceased pharaoh from taking revenge from the afterlife, they didn't destroy the whole statue. They simply smashed the nose. By cutting off the nose, they effectively suffocated the spirit, killing its power forever. Do you think this ancient superstition actually worked, or was it just vandalism? Hit follow for more bizarre history secrets.
